full_judgment: 23. Having gone through the relevant papers it also appears that the case property has been made waqf property by the Waqif Karam Ali Khan by a registered deed of Waqf in the year 1921 A.D. and within the relevant list of Waqf Administrator of the year 1946 A.D. the suit property has been enlisted. Admittedly the S.A. record of right stands recorded in the names of the legal heirs of Waqif Karam Ali Khan and the heirs of the wag if according to the deed of waqf became motuwallies jointly to look after the property. The learned court below in his observation and findings evaluating the connected documents, conclusively held that the kabuliat as alleged from the side of the petitioners and the filing of so called Rent Suit No.1788 of 1958 and the subsequent sole decree obtained in Title Suit No. 02 of 1972, which are under challenge have got no legal footings, inasmuch as; by way of registered waqf deed of the year 1921 the property has became waqf property and in this context; the learned Advocate on behalf of the opposite parties rightly cited the decision reported in 2 SCC 642. In the Case of Sayyed Ali and others —vs.- A.P. wakf Board, Hyderabad and others, their lordships held that, "a waqf is a permanent dedication of property for purposes recognized by Muslim law as pious, religious or charitable and property having been found as waqf would always retain its character as a waqf In other words, once a waqf always a waqf and the grant of patta in favour of Mokhasadar under the Mums Act does not, in any mariner, nullify the earlier dedication made of the property constituting the same as wave; After a waqf has been created, it continues to be so for all time to come and further continues to be governed by the provisions of the waqf Act and a grant of patta in favour of Mokhasadar does not affect the original character of the waqf property. "
